state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think the range wouldn't change if all the plants were cut in half or grew by the same amount? How does changing the values proportionally affect the spread of the data?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think if you cut all the plants in half, the biggest and smallest plants would still be the same distance apart, so the range wouldn't change. But I'm not sure about Katie's idea. If they all grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \), wouldn't that change the heights and the range too? Can you help me understand how the range works when you change the values?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: So, you're saying that cutting all the plants in half would keep the biggest and smallest plants the same distance apart. Can you think of a scenario where changing all the values by the same proportion would actually affect the range?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess if I think about it, if I cut all the plants in half, the biggest and smallest would still be the same distance apart, but maybe if I added the same amount like Katie said, it would change the range because the heights would all go up. I'm still a bit confused about how changing things by a proportion works. Can you explain more about how that affects the range?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks questions but fails to correct the student's fundamental misconception (confusing proportional change with additive change), and by Turn 4 the student still incorrectly believes cutting in half keeps the range unchanged while showing no real progress toward understanding.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses probing questions consistently, but fails to employ counterexamples to expose the student's flawed reasoning about proportional changes versus additive changes, and doesn't guide the student to discover the correct answer through more targeted questioning.
